prompt_boundary.prompt: Import externally produced implementation evidence for the scoped Beacon feature. Read Beacon source of truth and bind the imported evidence to the frozen PRD, user-story, and test-case truth. Implement only against the frozen PRD, user-story, and test-case truth above. Evidence refs: tests/test_v151_truth_map.py::test_implement_version_governance_preflight_blocks_metadata_branch_drift, docs/beacon/v1.5.1/features/beacon-truth-map-center-and-package-cutover/truth.md, docs/beacon/v1.5.1/execution/implementation-plan-beacon-truth-map-center-and-package-cutover.md. Changed files or service directories: beacon/utils/truth_map.py, beacon/commands/implement/commands.py, tests/test_v151_truth_map.py, docs/beacon/v1.5.1/features/beacon-truth-map-center-and-package-cutover/tasks.md.

items.text: `beacon.utils.truth_map` exists and exposes resolver APIs for feature truth package paths.
Generated truth-map JSON is marked projection/diagnostic and cannot be accepted as authoritative input.
Feature package Markdown carries enough contract markers for v1.5.2 canonical promotion.
Resolver exposes stable constants for source model and parser contracts.
New truth consumers call resolver APIs instead of constructing legacy truth paths.
Skill templates instruct LLMs to read truth map and feature package before legacy artifacts.
QA must not require an equivalent JSON projection for every Markdown truth document.
Doctor route can rebuild legacy triptych from feature package or reports unsupported gaps explicitly.
Change route can absorb legacy triptych into feature package or reports unsupported gaps explicitly.
Verify command fails or warns when resolver output disagrees with package files or rebuild metadata.
Truth-map route can rebuild requirement-derived `.machine` JSON from resolver-selected Markdown.
Generated machine JSON is labeled as generated state/evidence, not truth.
Generated machine JSON records resolver contract, source paths, and source hashes.
Runtime/process JSON is allowed without Markdown twins and is not requirement authority.
Verify fails closed when `.machine` JSON is stale, non-resolver-generated, or source-hash mismatched.
Resolver resolves version governance truth in addition to feature package truth.
Resolver classifies feature truth, version governance truth, generated governance state, and runtime/process records.
Manifest/index/cache JSON is never accepted as truth authority.
Material audit reads through resolver before using manifest or old paths.
QA, release, and status read governance truth through resolver-first routes.
Missing governance truth or drifted generated governance state fails closed.
Version governance materials are not moved into `features/<slug>/`.
Generated governance JSON/state carries non-authority labels or equivalent declarations.

Implement plan/dev-run surfaces verify version governance metadata branch contract before planning or execution, and fail closed when metadata, current branch, and git workflow expected branch disagree.
Implement current frozen revision

role_semantics.team_reviewer: checks implementation/spec drift before Ralph or QA closure
role_semantics.team_tester: checks implementation evidence and verification readiness before Ralph or QA closure
role_semantics.ralph: post-freeze controller that drives next-action routing across implementation, review, qa, and release

planner.purpose: Compile execution-ready task scope from the frozen revision baseline.

implementation-architect.purpose: Translate frozen requirement truth into implementation-safe module boundaries and service ownership guidance.

implementer.purpose: Write code inside the frozen scope and the implementation architecture note.

reviewer.purpose: Review implementation/spec drift and architecture-boundary drift.

tester.purpose: Check implementation evidence and verification readiness before acceptance.

implementation_preflight: Before implementation, verify the target service belongs to: .
Before implementation, verify the current branch is beacon/v1.5.1.
If a branch switch is needed and the worktree is dirty, stop and clean or stash first.

inputs_contract: conditionally required `prototype` when the feature has real UX/UI handoff
current gate / blocked reason / branch or execution governance context when present
`PRODUCT.md` — project-level product truth; must-read when the file exists at the project root
`DESIGN.md` — project-level design truth (colors, typography, spacing, tokens, Do's & Don'ts); must-read when the file exists at the project root
`docs/beacon/<version>/design/*` — version-wide design contracts (style, component-system, interaction-contract, state-matrix); must-read when they exist
`src/App.vue` or equivalent global CSS variable root — for projects with a design system, implement must reference existing CSS variables instead of hardcoding visual values
decision_protocol: Enter `implement` only after requirement truth is frozen enough for execution.
Block when frozen truth requires `change`, when cutover guardrails fail, or when a conditionally triggered prototype is still missing.

When `PRODUCT.md` or `DESIGN.md` exists at the project root, read both before starting any implementation that touches UI, visual design, or user-facing behavior. Treat them as binding design contracts, not optional reference material.
Keep `implement` as the only execution entry; `ask --execute` and support surfaces may route here but must not replace it.
Prefer explanation and routing logic in skill surface; keep final schema, contract, and gate writes in Python guardrails.
When dual-read or compatibility windows exist, fail closed on mismatch.
anti_inertia_notes: `implement` is not permission to rewrite requirement truth.
`goal`, task ledgers, or partial execution progress do not define completion truth.
If the feature needs UX/UI handoff and prototype is triggered, do not skip straight into coding.
Team/runtime internals stay internal unless the user explicitly asks for them.

When `PRODUCT.md` or `DESIGN.md` exists at the project root, `implement` must read them before building any UI. Skipping design truth is a process drift that produces implementation-to-design mismatch.
`implement` cannot rewrite frozen truth or override gate truth by itself.
learning_notes: Reuse implementation learning to avoid repeated blocked paths or flaky cutovers.
Learning may shape route explanation and caution, but cannot override gate truth.
Downgrade stale learning instead of silently trusting it.
backstop_cli: `beacon qa ...` after implementation evidence is ready
decision_surface.primary_reason: Enter `implement` only after requirement truth is frozen enough for execution.
